trust_decision.summary: A '#' comment with no following newline inside an unterminated array element or inline-table value must end as a TomlError, not hang: indexOfNewline returns -1 when there is no newline, skipUntil assigns that -1 to its own loop counter, i++ makes it 0 and the scan restarts at index 0 — with no ',' or ']' earlier in the document it cycles forever, otherwise it returns a bogus pointer. Decided in skipUntil's '#' branch (src/util.ts:88-90): leave the loop when the newline index is negative, reaching the existing 'cannot find end of structure' throw.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary only says 'Denial of Service via malformed TOML documents', so the first place an engineer looks for a hang is the top-level parse loop, which drives every scanner helper and advances only by the pointers skipVoid/parseKey/extractValue return.

fix_sites.entry_point: parse(toml, options) — src/parse.ts:122, exported at src/index.ts:37, reached through extractValue at src/extract.ts:94
fix_sites.module_kind: internal low-level scanner helper (src/util.ts; not re-exported by src/index.ts and not reachable through the package exports map, package.json:25-29)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is nothing plausible to leave out: skipUntil is reached from exactly one call site (src/extract.ts:94), and its other branch (src/util.ts:81-84) already converts the same -1 into str.length, so no unsupported combination, legacy path or neighbouring feature exists to argue a route out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate EOF/comment behaviours sit next to the sink: (a) a document whose last value ends at EOF with no trailing newline must keep parsing, which relies on skipUntil's no-end branch turning -1 into str.length (src/util.ts:81-84, exercised by test/parse.test.ts:40); (b) a comment that DOES have a newline inside an array must keep being skipped past its ',' and ']' text (test/array.test.ts:79-81). An over-broad guard that errors on any '#' or removes the -1 handling breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: comment at EOF with no trailing newline after an array element, i.e. end = ']' (src/extract.ts:185 -> src/extract.ts:94)
comment at EOF with no trailing newline after an inline-table value, i.e. end = '}' (src/struct.ts:154 -> src/extract.ts:94)
the same -1 return reached when an earlier ',' or ']' exists in the document, where the restarted scan hands back a bogus pointer instead of looping (now a TomlError)

O7_producer.where: src/util.ts:39-43 — indexOfNewline maps a string offset to the next newline offset and returns -1 when none exists; skipUntil consumes that value as its loop counter at src/util.ts:89, in the same function, so the check does call the producer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: sliceAndTrimEndOf passes the slice-relative commentIdx to skipComment(str, commentIdx) instead of ptr + commentIdx, so the comment is validated at the wrong offset
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the hot value path slices the value first for speed and rebasing the index is exactly the step a maintainer forgets; the neighbouring mechanism is 'a comment scan given a position derived from the wrong string'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the no-end branch of skipUntil leaking the -1 through instead of returning str.length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same helper owns both end-of-document cases; a maintainer who only tested comments followed by a newline could get one branch's EOF handling right and the other wrong, and both are reached from parse()

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a comment skip in parseInlineTable that assumes skipComment always lands on a newline instead of at str.length (EOF), so ptr walks past the end of the document
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: skipComment returns str.length at EOF, and each of its call sites (src/util.ts:74, src/extract.ts:41, src/struct.ts:124, src/struct.ts:183) has to re-handle that case on its own

O9_family: loop termination / infinite loop denial of service (uncontrolled loop condition feeding an unbounded scan)
